title: Sulfur, Right There All Along
body_text: Here’s one that I wouldn’t have expected. Sulfur is of course an absolutely necessary element for life-as-we-know-it, what with key molecules like cysteine, glutathione, methionine, biotin, taurine, coenzyme A, S-adenosylmethionine, iron-sulfur protein sites and many, many more. So there are plenty of biochemical systems for uptake, production, storage, and handling of these molecules and their precursors. But somehow we have missed an important one until now! Well, in mammals like us, anyway. It turns out that we actually store and use elemental sulfur as S8, the ring-shaped “octasulfur” form that is the bright-yellow form of the element that is often seen in nature and as a result of mining, oil refining, and so on. It was already known that prokaryotes handle sulfur in this form, but no one had seen it in higher animals until now. But perhaps that’s because no one looked closely enough? These authors were able to detect the S8 signature using Raman spectroscopy, and by using a mass spec method that involves capture of the molecule in a host-guest form in a polyaromatic capsule structure. That technique reproduces the detection of S8 in sulfur-sequestering bacteria, but it also shows that the molecule is found in human mitochondria and in cellular lipid droplets. Interestingly, its levels were higher in cancerous tissue (100mM or more!) The estimate is that a normal human carries around tens of grams (at least) of elemental sulfur in their cells, and we never realized it until now. One speculation is that it’s acting as an antioxidant, perhaps as a backstop to glutathione. The hydrophobic nature of the molecules suggests prevention of lipid peroxidation as a likely function, and cellular assays do suggest that as well. The authors also present a good amount of data suggesting that it’s synthesized by the actions of endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS), as an independent product of that enzyme system. This sort of thing always catches me eye, because it shows (yet again) how much we’re missing about what is happening in living cells. And if you think that we must be getting close to the end of having such surprises, that surely we’re about got it figured out by now, then I would ask you to contact me about some very interesting investment ideas. You’ll love those too!
